result.keyword: What's the best HR software for a small company?
result.markdown:
For a small company, my top recommendation would be **BambooHR or Rippling**, depending on how much HR functionality you need. If you're looking for something affordable and straightforward, I'd also consider Zoho People.

The best choice depends on whether you need employee management, payroll, scheduling, performance reviews, or all of those together.

## My top 5 HR software recommendations for 2026



**1\. BambooHR**

(Best overall for HR)

- Employee records and documents
- Onboarding and offboarding
- Vacation and time-off tracking
- Performance reviews
- Reporting and employee management

Best for companies wanting a proper HR department system without unnecessary complexity.

Pricing: Quote-based; small-company minimums may apply.

[BambooHR website](https://www.bamboohr.com/)

---

![#1 Workforce Management System - Gong Collective](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/6qeGsApk2jIdFyoxTSygvm7DexVcRwsdAMy-654nhQtsS9qblmlI3_rlyRsZYYkAZppbxudJa7sWDHqPbmVa4ApGBm0HQ-Ug4zK3bKSWGz9BUa-Xw79ufdKKevGKKSwz6wXnJf7tmhQAv7jp_2IhhmpGMf4r2A4gxIyk--T1g2YbjSd8UAKymDETIYyyT6m-?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. Rippling**

(Best all-in-one platform)

- HR and employee management
- Payroll and benefits
- Onboarding automation
- App and IT management
- Employee data and workflows

Best for a growing company that wants to automate as much administration as possible.

Pricing: Starts around \$8/employee/month plus a base fee; modules cost extra.

[Rippling website](https://www.rippling.com/)

---

![Introducing Zoho People 5.0 | Streamlined & secure HR software](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/N2tyoCYDXo_2X8HD_5-SWCfDBpBrfnJxvS27zq0luRDcSBxvb5ksF8GIcSrns-PjyFB81AcM6r9iE-CSXiUONYeUFYVq66I46rVVwsJXPLlWkRDDpj17x51dneUMDGMOeIbB1fDSAq7EtcK5moqwY1sb0xYonWwdnsoigFpIV0zzd1uQR8FzhmzsLBPdP8qA?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. Zoho People**

(Best budget option)

- Employee database
- Leave management
- Attendance tracking
- Performance management
- HR workflows

Best for smaller companies that want useful HR functionality without spending a fortune.

Pricing: Free entry-level option; paid plans start around \$1.50/user/month in some markets.

[Zoho People website](https://www.zoho.com/people/)

---

![Employment Hero Logo & Brand Assets (SVG, PNG and vector) - Brandfetch](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/Z6qVhSSYF5CYFaR38tVZ9vpu364SrI1qcU-LhtFo5MrKvM2IIECP5NGDLvCA9qSi3OHN3nIGoWj3sOAoSGJ3TbpMzqye4Jq3Q2-1Ae4X05g3VDo154uJn7RkzUUAY3Xfi51rzm16rZPnUZ2NnrKj1KHaQU4ePGT94fhowd8mNNeyff58VJ3Le5GJh2e89NE4?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. Employment Hero**

- HR management
- Employee onboarding
- Leave and attendance
- Performance management
- Employment documentation

Worth considering for Canadian or international businesses, subject to local payroll and compliance coverage.

[Employment Hero website](https://employmenthero.com/)

---

![Gusto: The all-in-one people platform for payroll, benefits, HR | Product Hunt](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/U9ihkiZChKRcgqjjRClvDRyT9XG9-GpMyinllUWob9alMftBmPGRcobY-YvDUQKw1cvVb4T3cEeJpN5ErI9IqBVMrrh8CobtTNAx_DYMZG5QgeYUTUHnLdeuUVTXGf9kQQbmuo-8rs3UnMu94W26KU8QJR6ha5lcvmllFK9LSsVoa23KAvlPVkN4pktlksyv?purpose=fullsize)

**5\. Gusto**

- Payroll processing
- Employee onboarding
- Benefits administration
- Tax documentation
- Basic HR management

Excellent for US-based small businesses, but not my first choice for a Canadian employer.

[Gusto website](https://gusto.com/)

These recommendations reflect recent 2026 comparisons of small-business HR platforms. ## Quick comparison

| Software | Best for | Complexity |
|--------|--------|--------|
| BambooHR | Complete HR management | Low |
| Rippling | HR automation | Medium |
| Zoho People | Affordable HR | Medium |
| Employment Hero | Broader HR workflows | Medium |
| Gusto | US payroll + HR | Low |


## What I'd recommend for a small Canadian company

If you're operating in Canada, I'd narrow the search to platforms that support Canadian employment requirements, payroll, tax deductions, vacation accruals, and provincial employment standards.

I would not choose a US-focused HR system just because it looks attractive or inexpensive.
